name: analog-clock
title: Analog clock
summary: Hour, minute and second hands driven by the clock, over twelve ticks drawn with a loop.
prompt: Draw a round analog clock face with twelve ticks and hour, minute and second hands showing the current time.
teaches: Rotate a hand around the centre with save + rotate(angle, pivotX, pivotY)
Drive the angles from the clock: (timeInMin() % 720) * 0.5 for hours, (timeInMin() % 60) * 6 for minutes, (timeInSec() % 60) * 6 for seconds
Draw evenly spaced ticks with a loop and a rotation by index (i * 30)
Set the shared stroke style and round cap once, and only colour and width per hand
Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre

snippets.note: twelve ticks: loop i, save, rotate i * 30 about the centre

check.describe: At 10:10:30 the hour and minute hands make the classic V and the second hand points to 6. Resized, the face scales to the shorter side and stays centred.

pitfalls: timeInMin() is minutes since midnight: % 720 gives the 12-hour dial position (0.5° a minute), % 60 the minute hand
timeInSec() is the second within the hour (0–3599), so the second hand needs % 60; a smooth sweep would use continuousSec() instead, which repaints every frame
Wrap each rotate in save so it doesn't accumulate onto the next hand

Don't rely on save/restore for the paint: the Java player's save only saves the matrix, while the C++ and TS players also restore the paint. Set every paint field a hand needs (colour and width here) inside its own save
The canvas has no background, so outside the dial it is transparent (white in the screenshot): add a background modifier for a square widget

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: literal coordinates sit in the top-left and get cut off when it is resized, so scale the drawing to fit (or derive positions from componentWidth()/componentHeight())
